## Chapter Twelve

Into the Shadows



Lucas awoke with a start as he felt a hand shaking him. “We have to go, we have an appointment” the old man said gruffly. With a groan Lucas sat up, steadying himself as his world went a little sideways. It took him a moment to steady himself, grabbing a few of the pills left from the now deceased doctor he finally made it out of bed and quickly dressed.

The two were in their air rocketing down the skyway along what used to be old Route 70 in Maryland within thirty minutes. “Where are we going Lucas asked turning from the view of the rolling Maryland hills to look at the old man. He never looked away from the skyline “We need to get you an identity, right now you’re a ghost and that won’t do, Dyson has plans for you kid” he said, Lucas cursed under his breath, that didn’t sound ominous at all he thought. They rode in silence for another fifteen minutes until Lucas’s curiousity broke it. “What was that you used on the doctor, that light thing?” he asked, remember the look on the portly old doctor’s face as the life drained out of his face and that little smoking hole in the center of his forehead.



“A cable cutter, its used in ports, kind of like a small powerful laser, it allows dock workers to cut through those large metal cables in an emergency” he said matter of factly as if the instrument he was talking about hadn’t caused the death of a man less then twenty-four hours ago. “Why wouldn’t you just shoot him?” He asked, thinking that might have been more human, or at least make more sense. Job smiled shaking his head. “You didn’t listen last night did you, Guns are available , as a law abiding citizen you can buy one, but they are genetically locked, they finally figured out the solution to most black market guns, if the weapon is not genetically tagged to you then it won’t fire and once you do fire, the barrel and bullet signature are registered, they know who shot the weapon as soon as they can pull the bullet and run it” he said.



“The one truth the corporations understood is that America would never fully give up its guns, and there removal of civil liberties happened over time, under the guise of protecting the people and the people wanted to feel safe, so they accepted it, But there are a lot of people who would have fought if they decided to remove all guns from civilians, so instead they made it mandatory, under the guise of safety to ensure any gun sold has a grip that can scan the DNA of the holder, and if that DNA does not match that of the owner, then it won’t fire, if you use a gun, you might as well hold up a neon sign” he said, shifting uncomfortably in his seat, the big man couldn’t seem to get comfortable in the driver’ seat “Bad back” he said without prompting and Lucas nodded. “We have had to get creative if the need to remove an obstacle arises” he finished, sending a small chill down Lucas’s neck, not a person, not a body but an obsticale as if they were nothing more then a speed bump, he hoped he never thought of people that way, again thinking of the look on the doctors face, the nice doctor who was so gentle with him, as the life drained from his body. The moment the man knew he was dying seared into the young man’s brain, it had not stopped playing over and over in his mind. He would give anything to forget that memory. He Left Job Alone and instead concentrated on the trees and farm fields as well as the old broken highway below.



A lot of the skyways were built along and above the remains of existing transportation arteries around the country, most had been ripped up and used for real estate the closer you got to the cities, but with almost half the population no longer present , the suburbs had shrunk bringing people closer and closer to the cities, the old suburbs that had spread out due to crowding and housing prices had gone the way of old mining and factory towns, most were dying a slow death.



Not long after that messages began to float over the center of the dashboard showing exits for Frederick Maryland. Job exited the skyway at the second one and began to descend to a small town that had definitely seen better days. The Main historic district was all but abandoned as no signs of life existed in the dilapidated shop windows of the line of granite and stone row buildings. Weeds grew up between the cracks of old sidewalks and broken windows welcomed them along with a faded black sign with white and yellow writing proclaiming ‘Welcome to historic downtown Frederick’. Lucas didn’t think there was much dining, shopping or arts left in the depressed area, despite the proclamations otherwise. Job entered a half collapsed parking garage, choosing to park the black car in the back of the first floor, Lucas wasn’t sure if it was to hide the car or because he was afraid it would collapse any of the higher floors.



They walked across an empty street and through a small opening between two buildings, Lucas surveyed the brick sidewalks, bridges and the canal in between the two lines of abandoned buildings. He could imagine that this had once been a beautiful place to have dinner or shop. He could see couples walking hand in hand along the brick walkways and bridges brining a smile to his face. His thoughts were quickly interrupted as Job pushed him a little “Move” he said quietly “We are exposed out here” and pointed up, as Lucas followed his finger, he could see the glinting of metal as drones patrolled lazily high above them.



Lucas picked up his pace and followed Job obediently, as they made their way across the brick thoroughfare and carefully over the rickety bridge over the canal. Moonlight showed there way as Job buttoned the top button on the large parka, trying to protect himself from the cold November wind.



The two made their way across a second brick covered fairway to a large building at the end of a row of buildings, all having seen better days.



Surveying the building Job turned to his young friend “Listen, because I don’t like repeating myself, and everything from now on is a lesson, is that understood?” he asked leveling that cold gaze on him eliciting a nod from Lucas. He knew the routine, Dyson had trained him and saved his life, but he was out of his element, he was now dead, his old life wanted and he needed to know how to protect himself, how to hide and most important, he needed skills he could use to thrive in this new world he found himself in.



“We operate on the fringe, we dwell in places that others don’t we are easily dismissed as the poor and homeless or druggies, we walk among those people that society ignores and by doing so allowing us to hide in plain sight, places like this” he said spreading his arms towards the half falling brick structure. Job approached and slammed his fist on the door three times, waited and then repeated the action. A minute later the large worn wood doors opened with a loud moan as the hinges protested their use. The two entered the dimly lit building. Where a tall lanky black man with a large mane of dreadlocks stood akimbo with a smile spread across his face. “Job, it’s been too long my friend” the man stated, Lucas noticing a very heavy New York Accent long coming out as lawwwng, Job embraced him “It has my friend, thank you for seeing us this quickly, Dyson appreciates it” He said invoking the name of Lucas’s old cellmate, which seemed to have the desired effect as the man stood up straighter and he nodded solemnly. “Please let him know I am always at his disposal, I still owe him for Philly” Lucas cocked his head, he wasn’t sure what he owed Dyson and he was pretty sure he never would, but whatever it was meant a lot to this man.



“This is T-bone Lucas, he is a good friend to have” Job said clapping the taller black man on the back. Lucas nodded and shook the other man’s hand. “nice to meet you” he said never really locking eyes with the man, the building spooked him, and he roved his gaze looking and remembering exits and egress points. “Well, lets get started” T-Bone said guiding the two over to as set of stairs that ascended to the second floor.



Once they reached the top of the landing Lucas could see a blue light that seem to bath the entire area and it wasn’t until they passed around a metal divider that he gasped, He surveyed the room counting close to seventy computers, monitors, printers and other items he could not even identify. Lucas turned to Job who was studying his face. 

“T-Bone is one of the best identity forgers we have access to , he is going to set you up with a. full identity, new Social Security Number, back tracked birth records, fully populated credit report and also fix that chip in your arm, when we walk out of here Lucas Christian will no longer exist” he finished and T-Bone motioned them in.



As he settled into a large mesh chair a very attractive Latina woman came over carrying a hot steaming cup and laid it on the desk in front of T-Bone. She nodded at both of the new comers. “Would you like anything to drink?” she asked pleasantly with a very light Mexican accent that seemed to add to her attractive demeanor. Both Lucas and Job declined, and she kissed T-Bone on his forehead and exited the room. Lucas followed her form appreciating how the woman’s backside moved in the tight-fitting jeans. When she had removed herself, he focused his attention back to the two men, both of which were staring at him with knowing smiles. Lucas felt his face turn red as the blush began to rise from his neck. “What” he asked annoyed. But no one took the bait, instead opting to focus on the work.



Lucas watched in amazement for the next hour as T-Bone Rapidly navigated through government systems and high security databases.



T-Bone closed the last of the screens and walked over with a device Lucas had never seen, the man expertly and gently placed it against his arm, and he watched as a progress bar wound its way to one hundred. “I have just set your chip to your new identity” he said and handed him a leather satchel a little bigger than a check book. “You will find ID, credit cards, social security card hell even a library card in there, giving you a completely new identity that will stand up to scrutiny, I have moved your DNA and prints as well as any collected biometrics from your original identity to your new one. Congratulations, you are now a new person” he said smiling and extending his hand. Lucas took it for the second time that night, amazed at how quickly his entire life had just been reset.



Lucas reached into the bag and pulled out the ID, he saw his picture and then read the name “Gavin Lock” he said trying it on for size. Then pulling out the other items in the bag, a passport two credit cards and yes even a library card. He smiled, stuffing them into his pocket. “When does that come off” T-Bone asked pointing to the bandages on his face.



Job looked between T-Bone and Lucas “Tomorrow I think, why is that going to be a problem” He asked, suddenly concerned. T-Bone shook his head “NO, I added a medical flag that he lost his eye in a traffic accident, so it will be fine” he was about to say more when the lights turned red and a small alarm began to flash on a black metal panel next to the computer he had been using. Surprised T-Bone looked over and then rushed to the monitor. “What’s wrong?” Job asked his voice was near panic as he looked around the loft as if people would jump out of the shadows at him. T-Bone began to flip through screens showing a grid of camera views , finally pulling up one to show a team of six people in black body armor creeping along what looked like the back of the building. “Shit” T-Bone hissed getting up, The Latina returned to the room and there host stopped looking at her, Even Lucas could see the guilty expression that hung across her features. “What did you do” he asked, but not in anger, just sadness. “What, they put out a bounty on anyone suspicious, and they have his description” she said pointing at Job. “Baby, the money they are offering, we could be setup for life” she said tentatively smiling at her boyfriend. He slowly walked over to her, hanging his head. “Oh honey, you shouldn’t have done that” he said gently putting a hand to her cheek and before Lucas could even react in one fluid motion, he pulled her head back and slit her throat ear to ear, her body dropping to the floor like a sack of flour. “Shit” Lucas whispered, staring at the corpse of the beautiful girl as the floor around her body became a red lake, He could hear the blood as it dripped between the boards to the floor below. Job pushed him, knocking him out of the shock that had been setting in “We need to go” he said. T-Bone nodded.



“To the basement, there is a tunnel that will come out about a quarter of a mile from here, I will buy you time” he said hitting switches on the panel as red lights began to light along the pillars and rafters of the building. Lucas looked closely and he could see boxes attached to those lights, he wasn’t sure what it was, but had seen enough movies to know what C-4 looked like. Job grabbed him and pushed him towards the stairs. “I’m sorry man” T-Bone said his apology sounding sincere. Job looked at him, then at the body of the girl and then back at his friend “You made it right” he simply said and then he and Lucas were gone barreling down the two flights of stairs to end up in a dark dusty basement. Job produced a small flashlight out of a pocket and with Lucas in tow he made his way across the room to the far wall. “We don’t have much time” he said urgently. As he searched the wall Lucas spotted a glyph scratched into the stone, an upside-down V with a keyhole symbol. He slapped Job on the back “There” he pointed recognizing a symbol like Dyson had showed him to look for. Job nodded and Slapped the brick with the glyph and an opening appeared next to it, just large enough for a person to go through if they ducked their head.



The two of them entered and ran down the long dark corridor. Despite the shock, Adrenaline kept Lucas moving almost overtaking the older man, the two burst out into a small woodshed and quickly exited it. Lucas looked off into the distance towards where they had come as a large orange blossom of fire erupted over the tree line. “I hope he got out” Job said and then bowed his head for a moment muttering something that Lucas couldn’t make out, but from the cadence of it, was probably a prayer for his friend.



Lucas turned to head back towards the parking garage, but Job quickly stopped him. “The car is blown, if they don’t know about it now, they will very soon, we walk” he said, and Lucas followed him as they both headed north paralleling the canal as they made their way out of the dilapidated city. “Why did he blow up the building?” Lucas asked, trying to comprehend the action. Job looked over his shoulder his eyes lighting at the orange light , still showing over the horizon “He bought us time, once she called, they had the area swarming with drones and satellite , scanning cameras and anything they could put their hands on, if we had tried to run , they would have had us in moments, by blowing up the building , he created a diversion, now all those drones are busy creating a perimeter around the blast site, the smoke and light gives us cover from the satellite as they are also concentrating on the fire, no one is out looking for us yet, but they soon will be, we have a small window to make it out of what we will there search perimeter” he finished as if lecturing to a student over a book passage, not about a sacrifice that someone had just made so they could get away. “That’s cold” Lucas whispered shaking his head.



Job stopped and turned on the young man “My friend just gave his life for ours, it’s not cold, we all sign on for this, we know what our duty is, he completed his, I will honor him for his sacrifice to our cause, it’s not cold, its honor, I will not mourn him until I am safely way, but don’t think for a moment I won’t weep for my fallen friend” Job said, the anger rising in his voice, and Lucas could see his moist eyes in the dim light cast by the little flashlight. He lowered his gaze and nodded at the other man “Im sorry, I just don’t understand” he whispered, looking to Job, his eyes pleading for the other man to explain it so he could, so he could resolve the deaths he had seen in the last few days.



With a deep sigh Job’s anger dissipated , I will show you, I will demonstrate what this government is capable of , but you will have to come up with your own reason to want to help, if you can’t then once Dyson gets what he wants from you, you can go, we need people who believe in our cause, not people who hang around because they have nothing better to do” he said, but all the heat was gone from his voice.



They followed Carroll Creek out of the historic district until it finally disappeared under highland rd. the two continued north for an hour on foot, passing mostly empty housing developments and in between swaths of woods and fields. Lucas crested a hill and looking across four lanes of broken and grown over blacktop stood a dark strip mall that hadn’t seen people in years.



Job was close behind him “This area used to be bustling with people, but after the plague, most moved closer to DC , once the population was culled, and the companies were annexed by the departments people moved closer to the cities as housing prices plummeted, so areas like this which at one time were a bastion for middle class families who needed to work near the district, but couldn’t afford property or rent there were no longer needed” he said as they made their way across the old highway, Lucas kicking over a metal sign , most of it had rusted over but he could still make out the Route 15 on the sign.



As they entered the parking lot Lucas looked over to the first large building to see a dark sign, some of the letters were missing but he could still put together the name “Wegman’s”. He wasn’t sure what a Wegman’s was, but from the looks of the building they probably did a lot of business. They passed through the large strip mall and continued north both men silent and lost in their thoughts.



Finally, Lucas broke that silence, as they were making their way though yet another area of woods, he caught up with the big man to come walk beside him as best he could, moving back only to dodge trees and bushes big enough they had to go around them. “Back there the woman said they were looking for someone with your description, how is that possible?” Lucas asked.



Job stayed silent as they crested a hill, conserving his energy to carry his bulk up over the crest. “Someone must have gotten a description of us from the doctors house” he said and left if at that. They hadn’t stopped so he wondered if a random camera had gotten a blurry image, with just enough detail to put out a general description, finally he dismissed the train of thought for another one “What did she mean reward big enough to be set for life?” he finally asked the other question that had been bothering him. Both men braced as a cold breeze blew over the ground. “The government keeps a standing reward for the capture of traitors or those involved in treasonous behavior, its a lot of money” he said.



Lucas thought about that, if he ever got made, everyone around him would be a potential enemy he thought, shivering more at the thought of what that would be like then the cold weather around him.



The two finally reached a development were half the houses had cars in the driveway and after a little while of searching Job chose an older model and quickly went to work obtaining it. He pulled a little device from his pocket that began to ping and chitter until Lucas saw the lights on the car blink on and off signaling the unlocking of the doors. They both got in and after another session of beeps, the car started, Job quickly rose the vehicle and left the housing the development behind. He pointed the car north and accelerated onto the main skyway into the District of Columbia.



Lucas was alarmed at first “What are we doing?” he asked, watching as, according to the signs the district was a mere eight miles out. “We are hiding in plain sight, right under their noses, your ID is clean, at least as long as all the computers in T-Bones house were destroyed it is, and Dyson wants you here in DC. Job said, his tone told Lucas it wasn’t a choice. Job landed alarmingly close to the old capitol building, it was no longer used by government and instead had been bought by the Smithsonian, He could make out the towering skyrise of the Whitehouse, standing forty feet in the air and the main seat of governmental power. As Lucas looked over the skyline, he could make out the present but shorter twenty story buildings of the various departments, all four of them bookending the Whitehouse tower.



As soon as the car landed in a public parking lot, both men got out looking around to ensure they had not drawn any undue attention. Following the older man, he watched as he pulled a device out of his pocket, one he had seen before while in prison. Job touched the button and Lucas could see the cameras in the parking area go dark. “What are you doing?” he asked looking to see if anyone else had noticed it and realizing the few people around were not even paying attention to them, much less the cameras.



Job continued to walk, making his way towards the corner crosswalk. “Ensuring that they can’t identify or track us once they find the car tomorrow” he said. “It won’t be a far stretch to figure out a car stolen in Frederick might have something to do with the raid last night” he finished. His head was on a swivel as they approached the intersection.



Lucas kept his eyes not only on the people but the cameras as well, as they came within thirty feet of any camera it quickly switched off, then on again once they passed. “How does that thing work?” he whispered, looking around to ensure no one else was close enough to listen. “A little gift from Dyson, it sends out a signal that over-rides the camera shutting them off as long as the signal is in range, it’s given to all top-level executives of the Departments, in case they need to ensure not to get seen. A wry smile spreading across his face as he looked back at the young man. Lucas shook his head; membership had its privileges.



They two reached Virginia Avenue and walked south, each one keeping an eye out for anyone paying them too much attention. Finally, after about thirty minutes of walking they reached the far edge of Garfield park. Lucas could see the twenty-foot stone wall stretching as far as the eye could see in both directions. After most of the intersections stood checkpoints. He had heard of these but had never actually seen one.



One of the first things the new government had done once taking over was segregating the cities by income. Most of the areas of the upper middle class to the rich elite were open and well groomed, protected by cameras and drones. But the other areas, the ones populated by the manual and minimum wage, the poor and the homeless were sequestered behind walls, it was easy to get into these areas, but hard to get out. As he followed Job the older man walked with a purpose towards the third street checkpoint. These areas were a no man’s land, no cops patrolled beyond these points and only the law of survival applied. Lucas felt the sweat on his back as the stories of lawlessness and killings echoed in his mind. The government had painted these areas as animalistic, cordoned to protect the rest of the country from the uneducated rabble that populated these areas, only let out to work the jobs the rich wouldn’t.



The stories of disease and death came to a crescendo like a song in his head. Through the break in the wall that was the checkpoint, Lucas could see the broken and crumbling buildings silhouetted as the sun set over the poverty block as it was known. Once beyond the wall the crumbling overpass once known as 695 still stood in sections, whereas in most of the city it had been removed, replaced with tasteful parks and houses. But as they approached closer to the checkpoint, it was like walking from the beautiful country of New America into the rotting corpse of what once was the United States. Lucas wanted to ask so many questions to protest to his friend to stop and turn around, but this close to the checkpoint with guards eyeing them he didn’t dare. He just fell in line following Job as he nodded to the guard and the gate was opened allowing them entry into the broken and battered neighborhood.



Once past the checkpoint, the guards now a distant memory Lucas walked up next to Job “Why are we here” he hissed, looking around as if thieves and murderers would jump out of any shadow and strike. Job nodded, never looking at his friend “Here we disappear, here the government doesn’t care what goes on, it’s here we can operate in the open without the fear of being watched or followed. It’s here where our efforts to resist the current regime is most needed, besides it’s a reminder of why we fight”.



As they continued Lucas looked at the once stately historic homes, now crumbling or collapsed, he could imagine this was once a beautiful area populated by statesman and doctors and lawyers. But now, now it was just a wasted and crumbling landscape. “How big is this?” he asked trying to follow the sightline of the wall. Job looked as if following his friends gaze. “From Pennsylvania to M and from third to eleventh streets. The cities poor and low income are squeezed into a five-block radius to basically live on top of each other. Every year it gets a little smaller as more and more property is needed for progress” he stated bitterly, like a jaded tour guide on his last tour of the week.



They turned on eight street Lucas watching as people walked among the ruined buildings, some working on putting a roof on what was once a stately brick townhouse. He witnessed a rough looking Latino male helping an old woman carry groceries up a cracked and half destroyed sidewalk and his fear turned to shame. “I had heard this area was savage and lawless, that going in here would automatically get you killed” he said to no one. But an ironic smile spread across Job’s face. “These are people, real people, not controlled by the government or puppets of the regime, these are the consequences of decisions made by people who will never come here, a man named Ghandi once said that a nations greatness is measured by how it treats its weakest members ” he said looking around.  Lucas didn’t know who Ghandi was , but he did like the quote.

Lucas felt shame at his fear, he knew there were rough elements here, and with no law , gangs quite probably ruled, but there was a gentleness to this area, something authentic about people helping people who didn’t have to , people giving some of the little they had to others who had less. The more he surveyed the broken townhouses the more he spotted little touches making them home the yellow flowers in a window, the thrice patched roof painted black with a happy face on it, the torn but clean curtains hanging in windows. These were homes.



They two approached the I street intersection when a boy of about twenty-two sprinted up from an alley coming to walk along the two of them. “Hello Rollie” Job said without looking at the young man. “Yo, J, Sally says to come see her tomorrow” he said walking casually next to him. Job just nodded “Okay, I will Rollie, this is Lucas” he said, the two nodded at each other Rollie’s face spreading into a bright white smile made greater by the darkness of his skin. “Hey man” he said and then in an instant he was off again.

They turned right and Job approached a large faded red brick building with a shop window covered in bars, the sign above the door simply said ‘Pawn’. Fumbling in his pocket he came out with a large set of keys and unlocked the six locks holding the door closed.

The big brown door groaned as Job pushed it inward and they both walked into the dark foyer.



With a practiced motion Job slid his had along the wall coming up with a light switch. As the room illuminated Lucas could see shelves of old electronics and cans of food as well as a case with knives and other various items. Above the case was an old yellowing linoleum counter that someone had welded rebar to make a cage around the area. Protecting what looked like an antique cash register sitting in the center of the old counter.  “Welcome home” Job said theatrically sweeping his arms over the store. Lucas felt underwhelmed though he wasn’t sure what to expect. It was better than the small cell he had shared with Dyson, so he kept the thought to himself and nodded. Waving the young man along, Job walked further into the shop to a door on the left of the counter, after fighting with another three locks he opened it, revealing the counter area walkway and a large backroom, filled with more of the old odds and ends. He walked back through the store room and through a door, this time without locks that revealed a narrow wooden staircase, the planks had been replaced recently but they still creaked as they made their way to the second floor.



Job opened the door at the top of the stairs and to Lucas’s surprise a large apartment with a fifteen-foot ceiling, the hardwood floors looked new and the counters could have rivaled any in the uptown condo’s of his friends from school. “Wow” he said at the stark contrast to the small dusty shop downstairs.  “What, just because we live here, do you think we live like animals, what did you expect a barn” he said another small smile on his face. Lucas shook his head “I, I didn’t know what to expect” he said walking past the open kitchen and the large dining table to the living room. Job pointed to a door on the right “That’s your room, get some sleep, we have a lot to do tomorrow” he said heading to the back of the apartment.



Lucas opened the door to the small furnished room and made his way to the twin bed, he hadn’t realized just how tired he was until now. And before his head even touched the pillow he was out.
